title: Receptionist
description:
Receptionist

Location: Cambridge, CB5 8 PA
Salary: Competitive, DOE
Contract: Full-time, Permanent- Monday to Friday (with participation in the weekend rota required)

About Peasgood & Skeates

Peasgood & Skeates is a long-established, family-owned independent funeral directors with a proud history of serving families and communities across Essex, Cambridgeshire, Suffolk and the surrounding areas.

We understand that losing someone you care about is one of the most difficult experiences in life. Our role is to provide families with care, compassion and professionalism at every stage, and our people are at the heart of delivering that service.

We are now looking for an experienced Receptionist to join our flagship Cambridge office.

About the Role

As our Receptionist, you will be the first person a bereaved family meets and will play a vital role in creating a warm, welcoming and supportive experience.

This is much more than a traditional reception role. You'll combine front-of-house responsibilities with a varied administrative workload, coordinating appointments, handling enquiries, supporting Funeral Directors and liaising with a range of external contacts.

You'll need genuine warmth and emotional intelligence, alongside the ability to remain calm, organised and professional when dealing with sensitive situations and competing priorities.

What You'll Be Doing
- Welcoming bereaved families, visitors and members of the public with warmth, dignity and discretion.
- Handling telephone enquiries sensitively, including initial calls following a death.
- Managing appointments, viewings and chapel of rest arrangements.
- Coordinating diaries and information between families, Funeral Directors and third parties.
- Liaising with clergy, celebrants, crematoria, cemeteries, doctors, coroners, florists and other suppliers.
- Preparing, completing and maintaining funeral paperwork and records accurately.
- Handling payments, invoices and account queries.
- Managing incoming and outgoing post, email and general correspondence.
- Ensuring reception, meeting rooms and public areas are maintained to an excellent standard.
- Providing wider administrative and branch support as required.
- Handling highly sensitive information with absolute confidentiality and in line with GDPR and company procedures.
- Supporting local community activities, events and fundraising where required.

What We're Looking For

Essential:
- Proven experience in a front-of-house or receptionist role this is mandatory.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- A warm, professional and empathetic telephone manner.
- High emotional intelligence and the ability to respond appropriately to people who may be distressed or grieving.
- Strong organisational and administrative skills with excellent attention to detail.
- The ability to remain calm and composed while managing multiple priorities.
- Competent IT skills, including Microsoft Office, with the confidence to learn new systems.
- Absolute discretion, integrity and professionalism.
- A smart and professional appearance and manner.
- A flexible, helpful approach and genuine commitment to providing excellent service.

Desirable:
- Previous or current experience within the funeral industry.
- Knowledge of Cambridge and the surrounding area.
- Experience dealing with funeral-related organisations or third parties.
- Experience in another client-facing role involving sensitive or emotionally challenging situations.
- Full UK driving licence.

A Role That Makes a Difference

This is a rewarding opportunity to become an important part of a team supporting families during some of the most difficult moments of their lives. The role can be emotionally demanding, and you may occasionally come into contact with the deceased, so we ask applicants to consider this carefully.

In return, you'll join a well-established family business with a strong reputation for care, professionalism and service, where the contribution you make to families and the local community genuinely matters.

If you're an experienced receptionist who combines professionalism with compassion, discretion and genuine warmth, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today with your CV and a short covering note explaining why this opportunity appeals to you.

No agencies please.

title: Administrator
description:
Administrator
- Location: Caxton, Cambridgeshire
- Job Type: Full-time
- Salary: £26,000 - £30,000pa dependent on experience

Reed are working with a great company who are seeking an Administrator to provide effective administrative and operational support at their depot/branch. This role is crucial for ensuring accurate processing of documentation, maintaining stock records, handling customer enquiries and supporting day-to-day business activities. The ideal candidate will have strong organisational skills, attention to detail and a commitment to teamwork.

Day-to-day of the role:
- Serve as the first point of contact for customers, visitors and telephone enquiries, providing professional and friendly service.
- Assist with processing customer requests, orders and general enquiries in line with company procedures.
- Support colleagues across the branch to ensure efficient day-to-day operations.
- Manage goods in administration, including processing delivery notes, stock transfer documents and ensuring accurate entry into company systems.
- Oversee goods out administration to ensure all products leaving the premises have the required documentation and maintain accurate records of outbound goods.
- Support the administration of stock transfers and assist in maintaining accurate stock records and inventory levels.
- Handle dispatch and invoicing administration, ensuring timely processing of delivery notes and accurate invoicing.
- Process credit requests and maintain accurate records, providing necessary information to Head Office.
- Complete end-of-day administrative procedures, reconcile payments, and maintain accurate financial records.
- Order office supplies, maintain filing systems and support the overall organisation and efficiency of the depot/branch.

Required Skills & Qualifications:
- Good computer literacy and willingness to learn internal systems and procedures.
- Strong organisational skills and meticulous attention to detail.
- Excellent communication and customer service skills.
- Ability to prioritise workload and work accurately under pressure.
- Positive and proactive attitude with a strong commitment to teamwork.
- Flexibility to support a variety of administrative and operational activities.

To apply for the Administrator position, please submit your CV detailing your relevant experience and why you are interested in this role.

title: Office Administrator
description:
We're excited to be recruiting for a proactive Office Administrator to join a brilliant team based on the outskirts of Cambridge.

This is a varied role supporting the smooth running of the business across administration, facilities, HR, social media and general office support.

If you enjoy being busy, are good at forward thinking and have great attention to detail, we'd like to hear from you!

In this evolving role, you'll be covering the following areas:

Administration
- Managing day-to-day administration, systems and records
- Handling calls, post, visitors and general office queries

Facilities

- Managing office supplies, cleaning, maintenance and external contractors
- Supporting general office organisation, including shredding and archiving

Finance & Employee Support

- Credit control

Marketing

And more!

We're looking for someone who is organised, reliable and confident managing a varied workload. You'll have good attention to detail, strong IT skills and a professional, friendly approach.

Ideally, you'll have worked in a similar administrative role, however training is available.

You'll have strong IT skills including MS Office along with being confident talking to people over the phone and in person.

Hours: Monday-Thursday 8:30am-5pm & Friday 8am-4:30pm

Salary: Negotiable

Benefits: 21 days annual leave, generous pension contribution, life assurance and free parking.

EA First Ltd are acting as an Employment Agency for this permanent vacancy.

title: Office Administrator
description:
Temporary to Permanent
Office Administrator
£28,000 pa - £30,000 pa
Based in Cambourne, Cambridgeshire
Mon-Fri 9-5 (office based)

Technical Team Administrator

Help keep great places moving forward

We're looking for an organised, curious and proactive Team Administrator to join our client's busy Technical Surveying team within a leading house building company.
This is a newly developed role, so it's a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys bringing order to a busy environment, solving problems and finding better ways of doing things.

You'll provide essential administrative support to the Technical team, helping information, paperwork and processes move smoothly across the department and wider business.
No two days are likely to be the same. From coordinating meetings and processing invoices to proof-reading documents, managing records and supporting the team with new processes, you'll become an important part of how the department operates, bringing structure and core processes.
And because this is a new position, you'll have the opportunity to make the role your own - developing and improving processes as the team grows.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Supporting the departmental meeting minutes, recording actions and helping to ensure follow-ups are captured.
- Raising and processing purchase orders and invoices, obtaining the necessary approvals to support prompt payment.
- Maintaining accurate records, databases and electronic filing systems.
- Collating documents and information and circulating them to colleagues and stakeholders across the business.
- Communicating with external stakeholders in a professional and helpful manner.
- Supporting the Office Manager with additional administration and overflow tasks during busy periods.
- Producing internal sign-off and approval paperwork.
- Proof-reading documents and assisting with the production of schedules and reports.
- Carrying out occasional drawing checks, with appropriate training and guidance.
- Supporting the team with printing, photocopying and other general administrative activities.
- Identifying opportunities to improve existing processes and helping to introduce simple, effective ways of working.

What we're looking for
You don't need to have worked in a Technical team before. We're looking for someone who is reliable, organised and keen to learn, with the confidence to take ownership of their work.
You'll bring:
- Excellent attention to detail - accuracy is essential, particularly when handling technical information, records and financial documentation.
- Strong IT skills, including good working knowledge of Microsoft Word and, particularly, Microsoft Excel.
- The ability to prioritise and manage competing tasks while working effectively to deadlines.
- Excellent organisational skills and a structured approach to your work.
- A positive, enthusiastic and self-motivated attitude.
- A natural curiosity and willingness to ask questions, learn and understand how things work.
- A practical, problem-solving mindset - someone who looks for solutions rather than simply identifying problems.
- Clear and professional communication skills, both written and verbal.
- The ability to work collaboratively and build positive relationships with colleagues and external stakeholders.

This is more than simply an administrative position. You'll be joining a technical team where your organisation, communication and attention to detail will have a genuine impact.
As the role is new to the department, you'll have the opportunity to:
- Help shape and develop administrative processes from the ground up.
- Build knowledge and experience within the house building and technical surveying environment.
- Work alongside an experienced and supportive team.
- Develop your skills and take on additional responsibilities as the department evolves.
- Make a visible contribution to the smooth running of a busy technical function.

You'll also benefit from a great office location, free parking and a friendly team environment.
We want this to be a workplace where people can do their best work and feel comfortable being themselves. We welcome applications from people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives.
If you're highly organised, enjoy working with people and information, and are excited by the chance to build something new and make a role your own, we'd love to hear from you.

Please let us know if I need to make reasonable adjustments to our process, please let me know about how I can best support you and make the adjustments that may be needed.

title: Personal Assistant
description:
Temporary Personal Assistant (Part Time)
Hours/days required: Preferably Tues, Wed and Friday, working 7.5 hours each day
Start: Early September
Location: Cambridge City (with parking)

Our Client, a well-established family-owned business with a heritage spanning more than 90 years. Operating within a dynamic and evolving industry, they have established a strong reputation for long-term, sustainable growth, integrity together with a supportive working culture. Recently, they have embarked upon a period of change to a new structure and are looking to strengthen the team. The Company prides itself on fostering a collaborative culture and valuing their team members' contributions. This is an exciting opportunity to join a close-knit team during a pivotal time of change, offering the chance to support senior leadership and make a meaningful impact.

This role is integral to ensuring the smooth functioning of the leadership team as they implement strategic initiatives and manage the day-to-day affairs of the business. Supporting the Executive Chairman and broader leadership team, the successful candidate will be at the heart of the organisation's transitional phase. If you're an experienced professional who thrives in a varied environment and enjoys working in a trusted, confidential manner, this could be the perfect opportunity for you.

Key Responsibilities:
- Managing and maintaining the Executive Chairman's busy diary, ensuring priorities are optimally scheduled
- Handling sensitive correspondence with discretion and professionalism
- Coordinating and preparing materials for board and committee meetings, including distribution of papers and follow-up actions
- Organising corporate events, such as board offsites and shareholder gatherings
- Supporting the leadership team with travel arrangements and expense reconciliations
- Providing administrative assistance to various projects, including preparing reports.
- Assisting with operational tasks within the family office, including meeting coordination and day-to-day support
- Contributing to office management activities, such as onboarding new staff, managing office systems, and supporting social and corporate functions
- Liaising with external agencies to support marketing and PR activities as needed

Essential Skills & Experience:
- Proven experience as a Personal/Executive Assistant or in a senior administrative support role
- Excellent organisational and time management abilities
- Strong communication skills, both written and verbal
- Ability to manage multiple priorities independently with high confidentiality
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office 365 suite, including Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Teams
- Experience supporting senior executives, ideally within a corporate or entrepreneurial environment

Desirable Skills & Experience:
- Previous experience supporting a Chairman, CEO, or other C-suite executives
- Business project coordination or event management experience
- Familiarity with SME or family-owned business settings

Personal Attributes:
- Trustworthy and dependable
- Approachable and professional
- Highly organised, proactive, and calm under pressure
- Flexible and adaptable to changing needs
- Strong problem-solver with a collaborative mindset

Additional Requirements:
- Availability to work three days per week, with flexibility in schedule
- Office-based position with no hybrid working preferred
- Valid rights to work in the UK

If you are ready to take on a varied and influential role during an exciting period of transition, we encourage you to submit your CV.

title: Customer Service Advisor
description:
A place to make a difference

Salary: £27,984 per annum, pro rata (£15.38 per hour)
Location: Peterborough, Hybrid, 2 days from home after successful probation period.
Details: Permanent, part-time position (minimum 15 hours per week) with flexible working hours between 9:00am and 3:00pm. Successful candidates will be required to attend a four-week full-time training programme (Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 5:00pm) before moving to their contracted part-time hours.

With over 21,000 homes across the country, we're responsible for supporting thousands of customers and their families.

We're proud to build positive, long-lasting relationships that go beyond housing. The work we do improves lives and creates vibrant communities where people of all backgrounds can thrive.

If you pride yourself on delivering the best customer care and want to use your skills to make a positive impact on families and communities, there's a place for you at Accent.

About the role

As a Customer Service Advisor, you'll manage repair-related enquiries, diagnosing faults and making sure our customers are looked after quickly and effectively. You'll deliver exceptional customer service, balancing their needs with those of our contractors and internal stakeholders, keeping everyone updated throughout the process. Your professionalism, efficiency and empathy means you'll build strong customer satisfaction.

Salary

The spot salary for the Customer Service Advisor post is £27,984 per annum, pro rata (£15.38 per hour) for applicants who fully meet the requirements of the post. If you're still developing some of the skills or experience, you can start at a salary 5% or 10% below the spot rate, with clear support and progression opportunities to reach the full amount.

About you

The essentials
- You'll bring experience from a contact centre environment.
- Proven ability to deliver high-quality customer service through clear, accurate, and empathetic communication.
- Resilient and solutions-focused when handling complex or challenging customer conversations.
- Experienced in accurately recording customer interactions using CRM and bespoke IT systems.

The desirables
- Knowledge of housing maintenance and repairs would support your success in the role.
- Evidence of confidently managing challenging customer situations and achieving positive outcomes.

Interview Process

We want your candidate experience to reflect who we are - a place to grow, a place to thrive, a place to be you.

Stage 1: A Place to Connect
A Teams interview with the hiring manager. You'll learn more about the role and team, and we'll get to know you - your experience, goals, and what you bring.

Planned Days: 16th of September

Stage 2: A Place to Show Your Strengths
You'll be invited to an assessment centre at our Peterborough office. On the day there will be role related assessments and a behavioural/scenario-based interview focused on how you apply your knowledge to real-life situations. You'll be asked to complete a Customer Service Questionnaire in advance.

Planned day: 23rd Septmber and 24th of September at 17:00.

The successful applicant will be subject to pre-employment checks, such as DBS and social media screening, before an offer is confirmed.

A place to build a future

We've got big ambitions and we're looking for people who want to grow with us. Here, you'll have the chance to learn new skills, shape your career, and thrive in a collaborative environment where your ideas matter.

And because we believe great work deserves great rewards, here's what you can look forward to:
Generous time off - 28 days holiday plus bank holidays, an extra day for your birthday, and the option to buy more.
Health & wellbeing support - Cash health plan, Health MOTs, online GP access, gym discounts, and a dedicated volunteering day for a cause you care about.
Financial perks - Car leasing options, salary sacrifice schemes, and exclusive discounts through our benefits platform to help your money go further.

title: German Customer Care Administrator
description:
Established over 30 years ago here at Lifeplus our mission is to be the world leader in holistic wellbeing by helping millions of people to unlock the wellness within them.

We manufacture and distribute high quality nutritional supplements directly to our customers all over the world. We are proud to have a team of enthusiastic customers and colleagues who are all dedicated to creating a legacy of wellbeing.

At Lifeplus we celebrate and embrace diversity and we believe that our success comes from creating a caring and fun community.

Job Purpose:

Our Customer Care Administrators provide excellent customer service to the network by building relationships, resolving queries on a wide variety of complex topics and processing orders and changes. Customer Care is the first contact point for our network and the role is to truly represent the values and principles of Lifeplus.

The role will include but is not limited to:
- Answer customer queries and process incoming customer requests via phone using Lifeplus Puzzel ticket management software in line with Lifeplus policies and service level agreements.
- Make outgoing phone calls to customers where appropriate in order to achieve a satisfactory resolution.
- Proactively develop relationships where possible, building opportunities with both new and existing customers and ensuring high levels of customer retention at all times.
- Ensure a proactive, flexible and positive approach at all times when handling customer requests.
- Participate in the ongoing development of Lifeplus Customer Care and the wider business, and proactively contribute to personal learning and improvement.
- Keep up to date with processes, and ensure a thorough understanding of, the company's business structure and product portfolio.
- There is no requirement to give advice on specific product recommendations.

Candidate Profile:
- Must be fluent in both oral and written English and German
- Passionate about delivering excellent customer service.
- Excellent IT skills.
- Knowledge of sales process and ordering systems is desirable but not essential.
- Excellent communication skills with both internal & external customers.
- Able to build good relationships at all levels with a positive and flexible approach.
- Able to solve problems, have initiative, and open to continuous improvement and learning.
- Must be positive, resilient, and adaptable to change.

Shift Pattern:
- Week 1: Monday to Friday. 07:00 to 15:15
- Week 2: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday. 07:30 to 15:45
- Week 3: Monday to Friday. 11:00 to 19:15
- Week 4: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday. 08:00 to 16:15
- Week 5: Monday to Friday. 11:45 to 20:00

Office attendance: 1 day per month in office

Salary:£28,000-£28,000 GBP

What's in it for you

Nourish your wellbeing: Every month, you'll receive three free Lifeplus products, plus 50% off anything else you'd like to try. It's our way of helping you experience the products you'll be proud to talk about.

Performance based bonus: Your hard work matters. Bonuses are awarded based on business success and individual performance, giving you extra recognition for your contributions.

Your growth journey - LIFE Programme: Our Customer Care Administrators take part in our structured LIFE Programme, designed to build confidence, strengthen skills, and support your career progression from day one. On completion, an additional increase of £2,000 will be added to your salary!

Learning at your fingertips: Access our Learning Management System (LMS) with all the latest learning materials and resources whenever you need them. Grow your knowledge at your own pace.

Peace of mind from day one: You're automatically covered by Life Assurance and Permanent Health Insurance as soon as you join. If you're ever off work long term due to illness, you'll receive 50% of your basic salary after six months, because security matters.

Holiday that works for you: Need more time off one year? Or prefer a little extra in your pocket? You can buy or sell holiday days to suit your lifestyle.

Exclusive colleague perks: Enjoy special discounts at leading brands and retailers, plus generous savings on Lifeplus nutritional supplements and wellbeing products.

Everyday healthcare support: Our Health Cash Plan (provided by BHSF) helps with regular healthcare costs, from dental and optical appointments to therapy sessions, plus hospital in-patient and accidental injury cover.

Little things make a difference: Fresh fruit delivered weekly, plus free tea, coffee, milk (including alternatives), filtered water, and fully equipped kitchen areas onsite.

Support when you need it: Our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) gives you access to confidential, professional support for mental wellbeing.

Invest in your future: Our contributory pension scheme offers up to 6% employer contributions, helping you build long term financial confidence.

A culture that connects: From team socials organised by your manager to our annual company-wide event (where life partners are welcome), we make time to celebrate together.

Eyecare support: We'll contribute £25 towards eye tests and up to £100 towards glasses if they're needed for VDU use. Plus, eye care vouchers are available to keep your vision in check.

Stay active for less: Save on gym memberships and take advantage of our Cycle 2 Work scheme to boost your fitness while reducing your carbon footprint.

Recruitment Referral Scheme: Know someone who'd love Lifeplus? Refer a friend or family member and earn £250 in cash when they join and a further £500 in cash once they pass probation. Sharing really does pay off!

title: Administration Assistant

description: Dynamic Health - Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy and Specialist Services are looking for an enthusiastic, self-motivated and dedicated individual to join our service. We have a permanent, part-time vacancy working 18.75 hours per week, Monday - 8-4pm, with the rest of the hours negotiable for an Administrator within our administrative team. The postholder will be required to support localities with unit wide working based at Hinchingbrooke Hospital in Huntingdon. Dynamic Health provides specialised community service across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, for people aged 16 years and over living with or experiencing problems from muscles, nerves and joints. The postholder will need to be able to work effectively to support the team to achieve deadlines. The postholder will require a good knowledge of administration and possess strong organisational skills. The postholder will be required to be proactive about collaborating with their colleagues across the localities and the Trust to problem solve and overcome issues as they arise. The postholder will be required to work using their own initiative and work on active improvement of patient pathways and wait times within the unit. 'If we receive a high number of applications we reserve the right to close this vacancy at any point after 4th September 2026' This post requires an Administrator to answer enquiries in a courteous and professional manner both by telephone and face to face, ensuring all messages and information is communicated appropriately. This will require the post holder to make an independent judgement as to whether the message needs to be dealt with by a qualified practitioner. Judgement will also be required to ascertain whether the message warrants urgent action. The postholder is required to be the first point of contact for patients both by phone and face to face on reception, to support patients by providing a warm and professional greeting to all and directing visitors and patients to the appropriate person or area. This will also include making sure the reception area is clean and tidy to adhere to the health and safety policy as well as infection control. The Administrator will work under the supervision and support of the Admin Lead to provide administration support to the localities within DynamicHealth. Provide office administrative support to the MSK Physiotherapy Service and MSK Specialist Service. Assist in the administration of clinics including booking appointments, cancelling and re-scheduling of appointments using SystmOne, ensuring data quality at all times. Answer telephone calls from members of the public, communicate information about the service, register the patients on SystmOne and arrange booked call backs for physiotherapy assessment in a courteous and friendly manner. Complete the accurate registration and administration of referrals into SystmOne, clinical patient administration system. Assist with monitoring of waiting lists and clinics for the weeks ahead and plan to ensure capacity is used appropriately. This includes sending online booking SMSs to fill routine appointments and ensuring patients that have been contacted have the process followed for contact and discharging appropriately for all relevant areas. Administer referrals from the electronic referral system, the self-referral system and the email inbox to include: Retrieval and attachment of clinical referral information.Registering the patients and referral opening on SystmOneAdding the patients to appropriate waiting list for triage and questionnaire sending. Maintain the waiting lists by: Processing the routine triage of referrals for all localities and pathways (Physio, Specialist and Pelvic Health).Responsibility for processing the urgent triage for all localities (Physio and Pelvic Health).Redirect referrals to other services, following clinical triage, such as referring to the community teams for physiotherapy.To support with the arrangements of relevant classes by sending invites and discharging patients who have not contacted as per SOP Receive, sort and distribute or action mail as appropriate via SystmOne emails, Post, Scanning, S1 documents inbox). To assist with the B2 task group and working through the tasks in date order to complete them in an efficient and timely manner. Tasks to include but not limited too routine letters, appt booking, Spec to Physio tasks, Community referrals, adding patients to the appropriate waiting list and sending emails back to patients and healthcare professionals. Maintain the Appointments for Booking waiting list and ensuring all the patients on the list are contacted and booked for an appointment in line with the process or time frame given. The post holder may be the first point of contact for patient complaints and as such would be required to be familiar with the Complaints Policy. The post holder will be expected to deal appropriately with these situations which may involve emotional and distressed patients. To support with the medicine management process for the bases, with receipt of delivery, adhering to the medicine management policy. Ensure photocopying / scanning is carried out appropriately and dealt with accordingly. Support with booking interpreter services for patients requiring a translator. Deputising for other members of the team in their absence, working across units or at other locations as required. To include providing cover for reception duties. Assist with keeping both manual and electronic management information systems up-to-date, including patient and staff information, ensuring accuracy, confidentiality and security of information at all timesIn conjunction with colleagues monitor and maintain the effectiveness of systems and processes and suggest/implement change when necessary. To understand the need to escalate issues through to the line manager to ensure problems are managed in line with policy. This includes reporting incidents through the datix system for investigation from the line manager. Support with the ordering of equipment and stock via the oracle system. Raise jobs with the estates team for any issues or concerns with the building. The post holder will be expected to prioritise their own workload independently and work to tight deadlines dealing effectively with enquiries from GPs, GP practice staff, other health professionals and patients. Communication: The post holder will be familiar with the Complaints Policy as the first point of contact for patient complaints, ensuring that these are dealt with appropriately and escalated as necessary. Liaise effectively with clinical, professional and administrative personnel including those from other disciplines, General Practitioners and associated staff. Liaising with patients, carers and the general public both directly and indirectly, in a polite and tactful manner, this may include dealing with difficult and aggressive people both face to face and on the telephone. Communicate effectively with patients including those with linguistic and cultural barriers both face to face and on the telephone including dealing with complex or sensitive information. To use information technology for communication including voicemail and email and for collecting medical data via SystmOne and the Choose and book system, reporting faults and problems with systems to the Information Technology technicians. Budgetary Responsibility: Assist with raising purchase orders, receiving deliveries and checking payments in line with policy and procedures. Observe a personal duty of care when operating equipment, moving deliveries and maintaining stock control. Requisition medical and stationery equipment as necessary to ensure availability in a timely manner and minimum stock levels maintained. People Management: Support other administrative colleagues with changes and expectations within the Service Maintaining own professional development and requirement to take part in appraisal and KSF process Support the admin leads when required with the recruitment process for shortlisting & interviewing. Clinical and Practice Governance: Observe and maintain strict confidentiality with regards to any patient/family/staff/records and information in line with the requirements of the Data Protection Act. Any data that is taken/shared as part of a phone call or transported, faxed or transferred electronically must be undertaken with regard to the Trust Information Governance and Information Security policies. The post holder must adhere to the Trust risk assessment and risk management processes The post holder must adhere to infection control policies and procedures Undertake mandatory training and any other training relevant to the role as required by East of England Community Health & Care NHS Trust. The post holder must participate in audits of working practices and patient satisfaction as required Provide patients and their families/carers with up-to-date information on standards they should expect from the team Participate in management supervision on a regular basis The post holder is required to participate in relevant emergency preparedness process for their team.

title: Medical Receptionist/ Administrator
description: Dr Laliwala and Partners are looking for an experienced or quick learner, enthusiastic and patient-focused Medical Receptionist/Administrator to join our friendly team at Nightingale Medical Centre. The successful candidate will play an important role in supporting the day-to-day running of the practice, providing excellent service to our patients and working closely with our clinical and administrative teams. We are looking for someone who is organised, flexible, a strong team player and able to work effectively in a busy GP practice environment. Previous experience within a GP practice or healthcare setting would be desirable. The Medical Receptionist/Administrator will provide an efficient and professional reception and administrative service to patients and the wider practice team. Main duties will include answering telephone calls, managing appointment requests, responding to patient enquiries, signposting patients to the appropriate service and processing online and electronic requests. The role will also involve updating patient records on SystmOne, processing registrations, data entry and supporting general administrative tasks. The successful candidate will work closely with clinical and non-clinical colleagues to ensure patients receive a helpful, efficient and high-quality service. Flexibility will be required to provide cover at our other practice sites when necessary. Job Description Medical Receptionist / Administrator The Medical Receptionist/Administrator will be responsible for providing a professional, efficient and welcoming service to patients, visitors and colleagues. The post holder will support the smooth day-to-day running of the practice and work closely with both clinical and non-clinical members of the team. The duties and responsibilities of the role will include: Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally, dealing with patient enquiries appropriately and transferring calls when required. Process face-to-face, telephone and online/electronic requests from patients. Maintain and monitor the practice appointment system, booking, cancelling and amending appointments as appropriate. Signpost patients to the most appropriate healthcare professional, service or source of support. Respond to enquiries and requests from patients, colleagues and external organisations in a professional and timely manner. Provide a welcoming and helpful reception service to patients and visitors attending the practice. Accurately update and maintain patient healthcare records using SystmOne. Read code information onto patient records where appropriate. Process new patient and temporary patient registrations and ensure relevant information is recorded accurately. Undertake general data entry and administrative duties as required. Process incoming correspondence and direct requests such as Subject Access Requests (SARs), insurance reports, solicitor requests and DVLA forms to the appropriate administrative team. Photocopy, scan and process documentation as required. Manage general patient and practice queries efficiently and appropriately. Support clinical and non-clinical colleagues with general administrative tasks as required. Maintain a clean, tidy and effective reception and working environment. Monitor and maintain the reception area and patient notice boards. Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with information governance and data protection requirements at all times. Follow practice policies, procedures and protocols and contribute to maintaining a safe working environment. Work collaboratively as part of the wider practice team and provide support and cover to colleagues when required. Attend practice meetings and undertake relevant training as required. Provide cover at other practice sites when required due to operational needs, staff absence or sickness. The post holder will be expected to demonstrate flexibility and undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role as required by the Practice Manager or Partners. This job description is intended as a guide to the main responsibilities of the post and may be reviewed and amended from time to time to reflect the changing needs of the practice.
